Md. Abdur Rashid & others
Vs.
Most. Amena Khatun and others
full_judgment:
15. Plaintiff No.6 is the mother of the plaintiffs 1-5 and the defendant No.1 Mst. Amena Khatun and as such she was the best and most reliable witness in the case to testify the veracity of the plaintiffs' claim but mysteriously she has not been examined in this case. Withholding of such an important witness gives rise to presumption that had she been examined she would not have supported the plaintiffs' claim which looked askance at the veracity of the claim of the plaintiffs. It appears that both the Courts below were inadvertent to take this important aspect of the matter into consideration. 

 17. There is a presumption of good faith in human transaction and who alleges bad faith such as fraud needs to prove the same. In the instant case, the plaintiffs were pleading that it was a case of fraud and as such they need to prove the same. Further, it was the plaintiffs, who wish the Court to believe in the existence or non-existence of a material fact. It was, thus, for the plaintiffs to prove the non-existence of that material fact, namely, the non-existence of the Heba-bil-ewaz deeds in question in the eye of law and, further if no evidence was led on either side it would be the plaintiffs who would lose. Therefore, on all counts, it was for the plaintiffs to prove the fraudulent character of the deed and this they cannot prove by the weakness, if any, in defence testimony. 

 18. Admittedly, the Heba-bil-ewaz deeds in question are registered deeds. It is true that registration of a document would prove its registration and due execution only and not the truth or otherwise of the contents or the recitals appearing in the document. Those need to be proved if challenged to be incorrect both as to title and as to delivery of possession. Though registration itself would not conclusively prove the truth of the contents of a documents yet the recitals in a document, admitted by the executants before the Registrar would create a rebuttable presumption as to correctness of the facts stated therein and the onus would lie upon the party alleging otherwise as there exists a general presumption of good faith and legality in all human transactions. 

 19. Since the plaintiffs allege the fraudulent character of the Heba-bil-ewaz deeds in question and also allege otherwise as there exists a general presumption of good faith and legality in all human transactions the onus to prove such allegations would lie upon the plaintiffs. But I find from the evidence available on record that although the plaintiffs examined as many as 4 witnesses in the instant case they could not succeed in substantiating the fraudulent character of the heba-bil-ewaz deeds in question as well as the presumption against good faith and legality in all human transactions and, thus, the plaintiffs have hopelessly failed to discharge the onus on them.
